newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Finance Minister admits not paying car tax.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Finance Minister admits not paying car tax.

text.p: Mexican Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz, who recently launched a crackdown on tax dodgers, admitted on Friday he had failed to pay one of his own tax bills.

Journalists covering Ortiz's arrival at Congress Thursday to present the 1997 budget noticed that his luxury station wagon was not displaying a current vehicle ownership tax sticker as required by law.
Asked about the omission during a radio interview Friday, Ortiz said: "In fact we have not paid the ownership tax." He said the "inexcusable mistake" would be remedied shortly.

Ortiz, whose ministry is running a series of high-profile advertisements on the theme "Pay Taxes - Don't Pay The Consequences", is the second high-ranking government official to be caught breaking the law this week.

Mexico City chief prosecutor Jose Antonio Gonzalez Fernandez admitted violating city laws by using his bullet-proof official car Monday -- a day it was not supposed to be on the road under an anti-pollution programme that requires each car to spend one day a week off the road.
